title: Unification of Upper and Lower Egypt
description: Narmer unifies the Two Lands, founding the First Dynasty and the pharaonic state.

title: Caral city flourishes in Norte Chico
description: Monumental pyramids and sunken plazas rise at Caral in the Supe Valley, anchoring the oldest known urban civilization in the Americas.

title: Austronesian settlers reach Taiwan's expansion phase
description: Neolithic Austronesian farmers in Taiwan begin the maritime diaspora that will carry language and outrigger canoes across the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

title: Early Dynastic city-states of Sumer rise
description: Uruk, Ur, and Lagash crystallize into rival walled city-states ruled by ensis, ushering in Sumer's Early Dynastic period.

title: First phase of Stonehenge begun
description: Neolithic builders dig the circular ditch and bank at Stonehenge on Salisbury Plain, the earliest stage of the monument.

title: Gilgamesh reigns at Uruk
description: The semi-legendary king Gilgamesh rules Uruk, later immortalized in the world's oldest surviving epic poem.

title: Old Kingdom of Egypt begins
description: The Third Dynasty opens Egypt's Old Kingdom, the age of divine pharaohs and the first great pyramids at Memphis.

title: Imhotep builds the Step Pyramid of Djoser
description: The architect Imhotep raises the first monumental stone building, Djoser's step pyramid at Saqqara.

title: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa flourish
description: The Indus Valley cities reach their mature phase with grid streets, brick drains, and standardized weights across a vast network.

title: Maya lowland villages take root in Mesoamerica
description: Early Preclassic farming hamlets spread through the Maya lowlands as maize agriculture and ceramics take hold.

title: Great Pyramid of Giza completed
description: The pyramid of Khufu rises, remaining the tallest human structure for ~3,800 years.

title: Longshan jade and walled towns in China
description: The Longshan culture produces eggshell-thin black pottery and fortified rammed-earth towns across the Yellow River basin.

title: Skara Brae village occupied in Orkney
description: Stone-built houses with hearths and box beds shelter a Neolithic farming community on the windswept Orkney coast.

title: Kerma culture rises in Nubia
description: The kingdom of Kerma emerges on the Upper Nile as a powerful African rival and trading partner to Egypt.

title: Sargon of Akkad founds the first empire
description: Sargon the Great conquers the Sumerian cities and forges the Akkadian Empire, history's first multiethnic empire.

title: Dilmun thrives as a Gulf trade hub
description: The island entrepot of Dilmun grows wealthy brokering copper, pearls, and goods between Mesopotamia and the Indus.

title: 4.2-kiloyear drought topples kingdoms
description: A severe multi-decade drought collapses the Akkadian Empire and strains Old Kingdom Egypt in a global climate shock.

title: First Intermediate Period fractures Egypt
description: The Old Kingdom collapses into famine and rival dynasties as central pharaonic authority dissolves.

title: Ur-Nammu founds the Third Dynasty of Ur
description: Ur-Nammu revives Sumerian power, builds the great ziggurat of Ur, and issues one of the earliest known law codes.

title: Mentuhotep II reunifies Egypt
description: Mentuhotep II of Thebes defeats his rivals and opens the Middle Kingdom, a golden age of literature and stability.

title: Lapita precursors push into Near Oceania
description: Austronesian seafarers settle the Bismarck Archipelago, laying the maritime foundation for later Lapita voyaging.

title: Indus Valley cities decline
description: Shifting rivers and monsoon failure drain the great Harappan cities as populations disperse eastward.

title: Assyrian merchant colonies at Kanesh
description: Old Assyrian traders establish the karum at Kanesh, leaving thousands of cuneiform tablets recording tin and textile caravans.

title: Minoan palaces rebuilt on Crete
description: After earthquakes, the Minoans rebuild grand palaces at Knossos with frescoes, plumbing, and vast storerooms.

title: Hammurabi takes the throne of Babylon
description: His code of law carves 282 rulings into basalt.

title: Erlitou state emerges in China
description: The bronze-casting Erlitou culture builds China's first palace complexes, often linked to the semi-legendary Xia dynasty.

title: Hyksos seize power in Lower Egypt
description: Levantine Hyksos rulers take the Nile Delta, introducing the horse-drawn chariot and composite bow to Egypt.

title: Shang dynasty founded in China
description: The Shang establish a dynasty renowned for oracle-bone writing, ancestor worship, and masterful bronze ritual vessels.

title: Mycenaean shaft-grave elites rise in Greece
description: Warrior lords at Mycenae are buried with gold masks and weapons as Mycenaean civilization takes shape on the mainland.

title: New Kingdom of Egypt begins
description: Ahmose I expels the Hyksos and launches the imperial New Kingdom, Egypt's age of conquest and monumental Thebes.

title: Rigvedic hymns composed in northwest India
description: Indo-Aryan priests compose the oral hymns of the Rigveda along the Punjab's rivers, the oldest layer of Vedic religion.

title: Polynesian-bound Lapita potters set out
description: Lapita voyagers with distinctive dentate-stamped pottery begin leapfrogging into the previously uninhabited Remote Pacific.

title: Battle of Megiddo under Thutmose III
description: Thutmose III crushes a Canaanite coalition at Megiddo in the first battle recorded in reliable tactical detail.

title: Mycenaeans take over Minoan Knossos
description: Mycenaean Greeks dominate Crete and adapt Linear B script to write an early form of Greek on clay tablets.

title: Akhenaten's monotheist revolution
description: Pharaoh Akhenaten abolishes the old gods for the sun-disk Aten and builds a new capital at Amarna.

title: Tutankhamun buried in the Valley of the Kings
description: The boy-king Tutankhamun is entombed with golden treasures, restoring the traditional gods after Akhenaten's heresy.

title: Olmec civilization emerges at San Lorenzo
description: The Olmec carve colossal basalt heads at San Lorenzo, founding Mesoamerica's first great civilization.

title: Battle of Kadesh between Egypt and Hatti
description: Ramesses II and the Hittite king Muwatalli II clash in the largest chariot battle ever fought, ending in stalemate.

title: Great Temple of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel
description: Ramesses II carves colossal rock-cut temples at Abu Simbel to project power over Nubia and honor the gods.

title: Assyrians sack Babylon under Tukulti-Ninurta
description: Tukulti-Ninurta I of Assyria storms Babylon and carries off its king, asserting Assyrian supremacy in the north.

title: Bronze Age Collapse engulfs the East Mediterranean
description: The Sea Peoples, droughts, and quakes shatter the Hittite, Mycenaean, and Levantine kingdoms in a cascading systemic collapse.

title: Olmec rise at San Lorenzo
description: At San Lorenzo the Olmec carved colossal basalt heads and built the earliest great civic center of the Mexican lowlands.

title: Collapse of Bronze Age palaces
description: Mycenaean palace centers burned and Hittite power dissolved as the Sea Peoples and systemic failure ended the Late Bronze Age.

title: Traditional fall of Troy
description: By later Greek reckoning the citadel of Ilios fell to the Achaeans, an event the Bronze Age world would remember as the Trojan War.

title: Zhou conquest of Shang at Muye
description: King Wu of Zhou shattered the Shang army at the Battle of Muye and claimed the Mandate of Heaven over the Yellow River plain.

title: David makes Jerusalem his capital
description: King David seized the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and established Jerusalem as the royal city of a united Israelite kingdom.

title: Solomon builds the First Temple
description: Solomon raised the Temple on Mount Moriah, giving the cult of Yahweh its central sanctuary in Jerusalem.

title: Chavin cult takes root at Chavin de Huantar
description: In the Peruvian highlands the temple of Chavin de Huantar became a pilgrimage hub spreading a feline-fanged religious iconography across the Andes.

title: Nok terracotta culture flourishes
description: On the Jos Plateau the Nok people sculpted striking hollow terracotta figures and smelted iron, among sub-Saharan Africa's earliest.

title: Phoenicians found Carthage
description: Settlers from Tyre led by Dido established Carthage, destined to rule a maritime empire across the western Mediterranean.

title: Hallstatt salt economy flourishes
description: Celtic chieftains of the Hallstatt culture grew wealthy mining Alpine rock salt and trading iron across temperate Europe.

title: First recorded Olympic Games
description: The games at Olympia become a Panhellenic institution.

title: Western Zhou falls, Spring and Autumn begins
description: Nomad raids sacked the Zhou capital near Hao, forcing the court east and ushering in the fractured Spring and Autumn period.

title: Traditional founding of Rome
description: By tradition Romulus founded Rome on the Palatine Hill, the legendary birth of the city on the Tiber.

title: Assyria destroys the Kingdom of Israel
description: Sargon II captured Samaria and deported the northern Israelite tribes, ending the Kingdom of Israel.

title: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem
description: The Assyrian king overran Judah and besieged Jerusalem, where Hezekiah's defiance and Lachish's fall were carved in stone.

title: Zoroaster's teaching spreads in Iran
description: The prophet Zarathustra preached worship of Ahura Mazda and a cosmic struggle of truth against the lie across the Iranian plateau.

title: Fall of Nineveh
description: A coalition of Medes and Babylonians stormed and burned Nineveh, bringing the Assyrian Empire to a violent end.

title: Babylon destroys Jerusalem
description: Nebuchadnezzar II razed Solomon's Temple and carried Judah's elite into the Babylonian Exile.

title: Thales predicts a solar eclipse
description: Thales of Miletus reportedly foretold the eclipse that halted a battle between Medes and Lydians, a landmark of rational inquiry.

title: Birth of the Buddha
description: Siddhartha Gautama was born at Lumbini, the prince whose awakening would found Buddhism.

title: Birth of Confucius
description: In the state of Lu. His teachings reshape East Asian ethics and governance.

title: Cyrus the Great takes Babylon
description: Cyrus of Persia entered Babylon and freed the exiled Jews, founding the vast Achaemenid Empire.

title: Persia conquers Egypt
description: Cambyses II defeated Pharaoh Psamtik III at Pelusium, adding the Nile to the Achaemenid realm.

title: Second Temple completed in Jerusalem
description: Returned exiles under Persian patronage finished rebuilding the Temple, reviving worship in Jerusalem.

title: Founding of the Roman Republic
description: Romans expelled the last Tarquin king and established a republic governed by elected consuls.

title: Cleisthenes reforms Athenian democracy
description: Cleisthenes reorganized Athens into demes and tribes, laying the institutional foundation of democracy.

title: Battle of Marathon
description: Athenian hoplites routed Darius's invading Persians on the plain of Marathon, saving the young democracy.

title: Battles of Thermopylae and Salamis
description: After Leonidas's stand at Thermopylae, the Greek fleet crushed Xerxes's navy in the straits of Salamis.

title: La Tene Celtic art emerges
description: Celtic smiths of the La Tene culture developed a flowing, curvilinear style on weapons and jewelry across Iron Age Europe.

title: Herodotus writes his Histories
description: Herodotus of Halicarnassus composed his sweeping inquiry into the Greco-Persian wars, earning the title father of history.

title: Construction of the Parthenon begins
description: Pericles commissioned the marble Parthenon atop the Acropolis as the crowning monument of Athens's golden age.

title: Peloponnesian War erupts
description: Athens and Sparta plunged the Greek world into a generation of war chronicled by Thucydides.

title: Zapotec capital rises at Monte Alban
description: The Zapotec leveled a mountaintop in Oaxaca to build Monte Alban, carving glyphs among Mesoamerica's earliest writing.

title: Trial and death of Socrates
description: An Athenian jury condemned Socrates for impiety, and the philosopher drank hemlock rather than flee.

title: Gauls sack Rome
description: Celtic warriors under Brennus defeated the Romans at the Allia and sacked the city, a trauma Rome never forgot.

title: Alexander ascends the Macedonian throne
description: At twenty, he begins the campaign that stretches Greek culture to the Indus.

title: Alexander defeats Darius at Gaugamela
description: Alexander the Great broke the Persian host at Gaugamela, toppling the Achaemenid Empire.

title: Death of Alexander at Babylon
description: Alexander died in Babylon at thirty-two, leaving an empire that his generals would carve into Hellenistic kingdoms.

title: Chandragupta founds the Maurya Empire
description: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda dynasty at Pataliputra and built the first great empire of the Indian subcontinent.

title: Euclid compiles the Elements
description: At Alexandria Euclid organized geometry into the Elements, the foundational textbook of mathematics for two millennia.

title: Maya build cities in the Peten
description: Lowland Maya raised the pyramids and plazas of early centers like Nakbe and El Mirador in the Peten jungle.

title: Ashoka embraces Buddhism
description: Sickened by the carnage of Kalinga, the Mauryan emperor Ashoka renounced conquest and spread Buddhist dharma across his realm.

title: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
description: The Alexandrian scholar Eratosthenes calculated the circumference of the Earth from shadows cast at Syene and Alexandria.

title: Qin Shi Huang unifies China
description: First emperor of a unified China. Standardizes writing, weights, and axle widths.

title: Hannibal crushes Rome at Cannae
description: In the Second Punic War Hannibal annihilated a larger Roman army by double envelopment at Cannae.

title: Great Wall linked under the Qin
description: Qin Shi Huang joined the northern frontier ramparts into a continuous Great Wall against the steppe nomads.

title: Scipio defeats Hannibal at Zama
description: Scipio Africanus beat Hannibal at Zama, ending the Second Punic War and Carthage's bid for Mediterranean mastery.

title: Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty
description: The commoner rebel Liu Bang triumphed in civil war and founded the Han dynasty, a golden age of Chinese imperial rule.

title: Rome destroys Carthage
description: In the Third Punic War Rome razed Carthage and sowed its ruins, ending seven centuries of the Phoenician city.

title: Zhang Qian opens the Silk Road
description: The Han envoy Zhang Qian journeyed west into the lands of the Yuezhi, opening the overland routes that became the Silk Road.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
description: Senators stabbed the dictator Julius Caesar on the Ides of March, hastening the fall of the Roman Republic.

title: Battle of Actium
description: Octavian's fleet defeated Antony and Cleopatra off Actium, clearing his path to become the first Roman emperor.

title: Rome annexes Ptolemaic Egypt
description: After Cleopatra's suicide Octavian absorbed Egypt, ending the last Hellenistic kingdom and the dynasty of the Ptolemies.

title: Wang Mang founds the Xin dynasty
description: The regent Wang Mang usurped the Han throne and proclaimed the short-lived Xin dynasty, launching radical land and currency reforms from Chang'an.

title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
description: Arminius annihilated three Roman legions under Varus in the German forests, halting Roman expansion east of the Rhine forever.

title: Death of Augustus
description: The first Roman emperor died at Nola, bequeathing the Principate to his stepson Tiberius after decades of consolidating sole rule.

title: Restoration of the Han under Guangwu
description: Liu Xiu defeated rivals and refounded the Han dynasty with its capital at Luoyang, inaugurating the Eastern Han period.

title: Crucifixion of Jesus
description: Under Pontius Pilate, during the reign of Tiberius.

title: Roman conquest of Britain begins
description: Emperor Claudius launched the invasion of Britain, landing legions in Kent and establishing the province of Britannia.

title: Great Fire of Rome
description: A six-day blaze devastated ten of Rome's fourteen districts, after which Nero blamed and persecuted the city's Christian community.

title: Buddhism reaches the Han court
description: The White Horse Temple was founded at Luoyang, traditionally China's first Buddhist monastery and a milestone of the faith's eastward spread.

title: Destruction of the Second Temple
description: Titus's legions sacked Jerusalem and burned the Temple, ending the Great Jewish Revolt and scattering the Jewish people.

title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
description: Vesuvius buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pyroclastic surges, preserving two Roman towns and killing thousands.

title: Gan Ying's embassy toward Rome
description: The Han envoy Gan Ying reached the Persian Gulf seeking Daqin (Rome) but was dissuaded from the sea crossing by Parthian sailors.

title: Cai Lun perfects papermaking
description: The court official Cai Lun presented an improved paper of bark, hemp, and rags to the Han emperor, revolutionizing the recording of knowledge.

title: Roman Empire at its greatest extent
description: On Trajan's death the empire stretched from Britain to Mesopotamia, its largest territorial reach before Hadrian pulled back the frontiers.

title: Construction of Hadrian's Wall
description: Emperor Hadrian ordered an 80-mile stone wall across northern Britain to mark and defend the empire's edge against the northern tribes.

title: Zhang Heng's seismoscope
description: The polymath Zhang Heng unveiled a bronze instrument that could detect the direction of distant earthquakes, a landmark of ancient science.

title: Teotihuacan's Pyramid of the Sun
description: The great Pyramid of the Sun rose over the planned metropolis of Teotihuacan, then among the largest cities on Earth.

title: Ptolemy compiles the Geography
description: At Alexandria, Ptolemy mapped the known world with coordinates of latitude and longitude, shaping geography for over a millennium.

title: Roman envoys reach the Han court
description: Travelers claiming to represent the Roman emperor Antoninus arrived in Han China by sea, the first recorded direct contact between the two empires.

title: Antonine Plague ravages Rome
description: A pandemic, likely smallpox, killed millions across the empire and claimed the emperor Marcus Aurelius at Vindobona.

title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
description: A massive Daoist-inspired peasant uprising erupted against the Han, accelerating the dynasty's collapse into warlordism.

title: Battle of Red Cliffs
description: The allied southern forces defeated Cao Cao's fleet on the Yangtze, cementing the tripartite division that became the Three Kingdoms.

title: End of the Han, Three Kingdoms begin
description: Cao Pi deposed the last Han emperor and declared the state of Wei, formally opening the Three Kingdoms era.

title: Ardashir founds the Sassanid Empire
description: Ardashir I overthrew the Parthians at the Battle of Hormozdgan and established the Sassanid dynasty, reviving a centralized Persian state.

title: Maya lowland cities flourish
description: At Tikal and across the Petén, Classic Maya kings raised temple-pyramids and carved stelae recording dynasties and wars.

title: Shapur I captures Emperor Valerian
description: The Sassanid king Shapur I defeated and took captive the Roman emperor Valerian near Edessa, a humiliation immortalized in rock reliefs.

title: Aurelian defeats Palmyra
description: Emperor Aurelian crushed Queen Zenobia's breakaway Palmyrene Empire, reuniting the fracturing Roman realm.

title: Jin dynasty reunifies China
description: The Jin dynasty conquered Eastern Wu, briefly reuniting China under a single throne after the Three Kingdoms' division.

title: Moche civilization at its height
description: On Peru's north coast the Moche built the great adobe Huacas of the Sun and Moon and produced vivid ceramic portrait vessels.

title: Armenia adopts Christianity
description: King Tiridates III, converted by Gregory the Illuminator, made Armenia the first kingdom to embrace Christianity as its state religion.

title: Edict of Milan
description: Constantine and Licinius proclaimed religious toleration across the empire, ending the persecution of Christians.

title: Chandragupta I founds the Gupta Empire
description: Chandragupta I united the Ganges plain and inaugurated the Gupta dynasty, ushering in a golden age of Indian civilization.

title: Council of Nicaea
description: Constantine convened the first ecumenical council, which defined the Nicene Creed and condemned Arianism.

title: Dedication of Constantinople
description: Constantine refounded Byzantium as the new imperial capital, a Christian city astride the Bosporus guarding Europe and Asia.

title: Aksum sacks Meroe
description: King Ezana of Aksum, having converted to Christianity, campaigned into Nubia and overthrew the kingdom of Kush.

title: Nazca lines etched in the desert
description: The Nazca people completed vast geoglyphs of animals and lines across the Peruvian desert, visible only from the heights.

title: Hypatia's father Theon at Alexandria
description: The mathematician Theon worked at the Museum of Alexandria, editing Euclid and preserving Greek science into late antiquity.

title: Huns cross the Volga
description: The westward surge of the Huns shattered the Gothic kingdoms, triggering the great migrations that would reshape Europe.

title: Battle of Adrianople
description: Gothic cavalry destroyed the eastern Roman army and killed Emperor Valens, a disaster marking the empire's deepening crisis.

title: Christianity made the Roman state religion
description: Emperor Theodosius issued the Edict of Thessalonica, establishing Nicene Christianity as the official faith of the empire.

title: Faxian's pilgrimage to India
description: The Chinese monk Faxian set out overland to India to collect Buddhist scriptures, later recording his travels across Asia.

title: Kalidasa and the Gupta golden age
description: Under Chandragupta II the poet Kalidasa flourished, while Gupta scholars advanced mathematics, astronomy, and the arts.

title: Sack of Rome by the Visigoths
description: Alaric's Visigoths plundered Rome for three days, the first fall of the city to a foreign enemy in eight centuries.

title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
description: A Roman-Visigothic coalition halted Attila the Hun's invasion of Gaul in one of late antiquity's bloodiest battles.

title: Vandals sack Rome
description: Geiseric's Vandals, having built a kingdom in North Africa, crossed the sea and thoroughly plundered the city of Rome.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: The Germanic commander Odoacer deposed the boy-emperor Romulus Augustulus, ending the line of Western Roman emperors.

title: Aryabhata's astronomical treatise
description: The mathematician Aryabhata completed the Aryabhatiya, proposing a rotating Earth and advancing trigonometry and the value of pi.

title: Justinian becomes emperor
description: Justinian I took the Byzantine throne and launched campaigns to reconquer the lost West and codify Roman law.

title: Nika riots and Hagia Sophia begun
description: After deadly riots gutted Constantinople, Justinian ordered the rebuilding of Hagia Sophia as the greatest church of Christendom.

title: Buddhism introduced to Japan
description: A Korean embassy from Baekje presented Buddhist images and sutras to the Yamato court, planting the faith in Japan.

title: Plague of Justinian
description: The first recorded bubonic plague pandemic swept the Mediterranean from Constantinople, killing a vast share of the population.

title: Birth of Muhammad
description: The future prophet of Islam was born at Mecca into the Quraysh tribe, in a city of merchants and pilgrimage.

title: Sui dynasty reunifies China
description: The Sui conquered the southern Chen dynasty, reuniting China after nearly four centuries of division.

title: Muhammad's First Revelation
description: In a cave on Mount Hira above Mecca, Muhammad reported the first Quranic revelation, marking the birth of Islam.

title: Founding of the Tang Dynasty
description: Li Yuan seized Chang'an and proclaimed the Tang Dynasty, launching an age of cosmopolitan brilliance across China.

title: The Hijra
description: Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina. Year one of the Islamic calendar.

title: Death of Muhammad and Rashidun Caliphate
description: Muhammad died in Medina, and Abu Bakr became the first caliph to lead the rapidly expanding Muslim community.

title: Battle of Yarmouk
description: Arab armies crushed the Byzantine forces beside the Yarmouk River, stripping Syria from the Eastern Roman Empire.

title: Muslim Conquest of Egypt
description: Amr ibn al-As took Alexandria and Babylon fortress, ending seven centuries of Roman rule over Egypt.

title: Taika Reforms in Japan
description: The Yamato court enacted sweeping Taika reforms modeled on Tang China, centralizing land and taxation under the emperor.

title: Fall of the Sasanian Empire
description: The murder of Yazdegerd III near Merv extinguished the Sasanian dynasty and opened Persia to Islam.

title: Umayyad Caliphate Established
description: Mu'awiya made Damascus the capital of the new Umayyad Caliphate, founding Islam's first hereditary dynasty.

title: Great Jaguar Paw Reign at Tikal
description: Jasaw Chan K'awiil I revived the Maya city of Tikal, raising towering temple pyramids above the rainforest canopy.

title: Dome of the Rock Completed
description: Caliph Abd al-Malik completed the golden Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, the earliest surviving Islamic monument.

title: Muslim Conquest of Hispania
description: Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed at Gibraltar and shattered the Visigothic army, beginning nearly eight centuries of Al-Andalus.

title: Great Mosque of Damascus Finished
description: Al-Walid I completed the Great Mosque of Damascus, its glittering mosaics setting a template for Islamic sacred architecture.

title: Battle of Tours
description: Charles Martel halted a Muslim advance into Francia between Tours and Poitiers, checking Islam's northward spread.

title: Battle of Talas
description: Abbasid forces defeated a Tang army by the Talas River, and captured artisans soon carried papermaking west into the Islamic world.

title: An Lushan Rebellion
description: General An Lushan revolted against the Tang, unleashing a devastating war that drained the empire of millions of lives.

title: Baghdad Founded
description: Caliph al-Mansur laid out the round city of Baghdad on the Tigris, soon the richest metropolis of the medieval world.

title: Charlemagne Becomes King of the Franks
description: Charlemagne inherited the Frankish throne and began the conquests that would forge a new Western empire from Aachen.

title: Viking Raid on Lindisfarne
description: Norse raiders sacked the monastery of Lindisfarne, a shocking strike that announced the dawn of the Viking Age.

title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
description: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor in Rome on Christmas Day, reviving the imperial title in the Latin West.

title: Jayavarman II Founds the Khmer Empire
description: Jayavarman II declared himself universal monarch on the Kulen plateau, founding the Khmer Empire of Angkor.

title: Al-Khwarizmi and the House of Wisdom
description: At Baghdad's House of Wisdom, al-Khwarizmi wrote the treatise on al-jabr that gave algebra its name.

title: Samarra Becomes Abbasid Capital
description: Caliph al-Mu'tasim moved his court and Turkish guard to the new palace city of Samarra on the Tigris.

title: Collapse of the Uyghur Khaganate
description: A Kyrgyz onslaught and harsh winter destroyed the Uyghur Khaganate, scattering its people southward into the Tarim Basin.

title: Rurik and the Rus at Novgorod
description: The Varangian chieftain Rurik took control at Novgorod, founding the dynasty that would rule the Kievan Rus.

title: The Diamond Sutra Printed
description: A Tang printer produced the Diamond Sutra at Dunhuang, the earliest dated complete printed book in the world.

title: Norse Settlement of Iceland
description: Ingolfr Arnarson built his farmstead at Reykjavik, beginning the permanent Norse colonization of Iceland.

title: Golden Age of Ghana Empire
description: The Soninke kings of Ghana grew rich taxing gold and salt caravans crossing the western Sahara.

title: Fatimid Caliphate Proclaimed
description: The Isma'ili Shia leader Abdullah al-Mahdi proclaimed the Fatimid Caliphate in Ifriqiya, rivaling Baghdad.

title: Rollo Granted Normandy
description: The Frankish king ceded land around Rouen to the Viking Rollo, planting the seed of the Duchy of Normandy.

title: England Unified under Athelstan
description: Athelstan took York and received the submission of northern kings, becoming the first ruler of a united England.

title: Otto I and the German Kingdom
description: Otto I was crowned at Aachen, beginning the reign that would restore imperial power and found the Holy Roman Empire.

title: Founding of the Song Dynasty
description: Zhao Kuangyin reunited China as Emperor Taizu of the Song, ushering in an era of commerce, science, and art.

title: Cairo Founded by the Fatimids
description: Fatimid general Jawhar laid out al-Qahira beside the Nile, soon the brilliant capital of a Mediterranean empire.

title: Christianization of Kievan Rus
description: Vladimir the Great was baptized and had Kiev's idols thrown into the Dnieper, binding the Rus to Byzantine Christianity.

title: Leif Erikson Reaches Vinland
description: Leif Erikson led Norse sailors to Vinland at L'Anse aux Meadows, the first Europeans known to reach the Americas.

title: The Tale of Genji Written
description: At the Heian court in Kyoto, Murasaki Shikibu composed The Tale of Genji, often called the world's first novel.

title: Ibn al-Haytham's Book of Optics
description: In Cairo, Ibn al-Haytham completed his Book of Optics, laying the foundations of the experimental scientific method.

title: Pi Sheng Invents Movable Type
description: The Song artisan Bi Sheng devised movable type from baked clay, centuries before Gutenberg's press in Europe.

title: The Great Schism
description: Mutual excommunications between Rome and Constantinople split Christendom into the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

title: Crab Nebula Supernova Recorded
description: Song astronomers recorded a dazzling guest star in Taurus, the supernova that left behind the Crab Nebula.

title: Battle of Hastings
description: William of Normandy defeats Harold Godwinson, reshaping English language and law.

title: Battle of Manzikert
description: Seljuk Turks routed the Byzantines and captured their emperor, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

title: Almoravids Sack Koumbi Saleh
description: Almoravid and Sahelian pressure broke the Ghana Empire's grip on the trans-Saharan gold trade.

title: Pope Urban II Calls the First Crusade
description: At Clermont, Pope Urban II summoned Christian knights to recover Jerusalem, launching the era of the Crusades.

title: Crusaders Capture Jerusalem
description: After a brutal siege, the First Crusade stormed Jerusalem and established the Latin Kingdom in the Holy Land.

title: Angkor Wat Begun under Suryavarman II
description: Suryavarman II began raising Angkor Wat, the vast temple-mountain that remains the largest religious monument on Earth.

title: Rise of Great Zimbabwe
description: Shona builders began the dry-stone walls of Great Zimbabwe, hub of a kingdom trading gold to the Indian Ocean coast.

title: Toltec Capital Tula Falls
description: The Toltec capital of Tula was burned and abandoned, ending a civilization later revered by the Aztecs.

title: Hohokam Canal Cities of the Southwest
description: The Hohokam expanded vast irrigation canals across the Salt River valley, sustaining desert farming towns.

title: Minamoto Victory and the Kamakura Shogunate
description: The Minamoto crushed the Taira at Dan-no-ura, paving the way for Japan's first military shogunate.

title: Polynesian Voyagers Settle New Zealand
description: Ancestral Maori navigators reached Aotearoa by double-hulled canoe, the last great landmass settled by humans.

title: Tiwanaku Decline in the Andes
description: Prolonged drought drained the raised-field farms around Lake Titicaca, hastening the fall of the Tiwanaku state.

title: Genghis Khan proclaimed
description: Temujin unites the Mongol tribes. The empire that follows reaches from Korea to Hungary.

title: Genghis Khan unites the Mongols
description: Temujin is proclaimed Genghis Khan at a kurultai on the Onon River, forging the scattered steppe tribes into a single Mongol nation.

title: Delhi Sultanate founded
description: Qutb al-Din Aibak, a former Turkic slave-general, establishes Muslim rule over Delhi and begins the Qutb Minar.

title: Mongol invasion of Jin China begins
description: Genghis Khan's horsemen pour through the Great Wall and besiege the Jin dynasty's capital at Zhongdu.

title: Magna Carta sealed at Runnymede
description: King John bows to his rebellious barons and seals the Great Charter, binding the English crown to the rule of law.

title: Mongols sack the Khwarazmian Empire
description: Enraged by a murdered embassy, Genghis Khan unleashes his armies on Samarkand and Bukhara, laying waste to Persia's eastern cities.

title: Fall of Baghdad to the Mongols
description: Hulagu Khan storms the Abbasid capital, executes the caliph, and casts the House of Wisdom's books into the Tigris until it runs black with ink.

title: Marco Polo departs for Cathay
description: The young Venetian sets out with his father and uncle on the Silk Road toward the court of Kublai Khan.

title: First Mongol invasion of Japan repelled
description: A typhoon the Japanese call kamikaze scatters Kublai Khan's invasion fleet off Hakata Bay.

title: Yuan dynasty conquers Song China
description: At the naval battle of Yamen the last Song emperor drowns, completing the Mongol conquest of all China under Kublai Khan.

title: Papacy moves to Avignon
description: Pope Clement V settles the Holy See at Avignon under French influence, beginning the papacy's seventy-year exile from Rome.

title: Great Famine strikes Europe
description: Years of torrential rain rot the crops and millions starve across a continent whose climate has turned suddenly cold and wet.

title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
description: The Mali emperor passes through Cairo distributing so much gold that its price collapses for a decade, revealing West Africa's fabulous wealth.

title: Aztecs found Tenochtitlan
description: The wandering Mexica build their island city on Lake Texcoco where they see an eagle perched on a cactus devouring a serpent.

title: Ibn Battuta begins his travels
description: A young Moroccan jurist leaves Tangier on a pilgrimage that will become a thirty-year journey across the whole of the Islamic world.

title: Hundred Years' War begins
description: Edward III of England claims the French throne, igniting a dynastic conflict that will scar France for over a century.

title: Black Death reaches Europe
description: Plague-ridden Genoese galleys dock at Messina, loosing a pestilence that will kill a third of Europe within five years.

title: Ming dynasty overthrows the Yuan
description: The rebel peasant Zhu Yuanzhang drives the Mongols back to the steppe and proclaims himself the Hongwu Emperor at Nanjing.

title: Western Schism splits the Church
description: Rival popes in Rome and Avignon excommunicate one another, dividing the loyalties of Christendom for nearly forty years.

title: Timur sacks Delhi
description: Tamerlane's army storms the Delhi Sultanate's capital and massacres its inhabitants, leaving the city in ruins for years.

title: Timur defeats the Ottomans at Ankara
description: Tamerlane captures Sultan Bayezid I in battle, shattering Ottoman power and delaying the fall of Constantinople by half a century.

title: Zheng He's first treasure voyage
description: The Ming admiral sets sail with a vast fleet of treasure ships to project Chinese power across the Indian Ocean.

title: Portugal seizes Ceuta
description: Prince Henry the Navigator's capture of the Moroccan port launches Portugal's drive down the African coast.

title: Joan of Arc lifts the siege of Orleans
description: A peasant girl claiming divine visions rallies French forces and breaks the English siege, turning the tide of the Hundred Years' War.

title: Aztec Triple Alliance formed
description: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan join forces to dominate central Mexico and build the Aztec Empire.

title: Pachacuti founds the Inca Empire
description: After repelling the Chanca, Pachacuti transforms Cusco into the capital of a vast Andean empire bound by roads and terraces.

title: Johannes Gutenberg develops movable type
description: At Mainz a goldsmith perfects a printing press with reusable metal type, making books cheap and igniting an information revolution.

title: Vijayanagara at its height
description: The Hindu empire's capital of Vijayanagara flourishes as one of the world's great cities, its markets heaped with gems and spices.

title: Fall of Constantinople
description: Mehmed II's great bombards breach the Theodosian walls, ending the thousand-year Byzantine Empire and making the city Ottoman.

title: Sunni Ali founds the Songhai Empire
description: Sunni Ali expands from Gao to seize Timbuktu and Djenne, building the largest empire West Africa had ever seen.

title: Union of Castile and Aragon
description: The marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand joins the great Christian kingdoms, forging the Spain that will complete the Reconquista.

title: Botticelli paints the Birth of Venus
description: Under Medici patronage Sandro Botticelli depicts the goddess rising from the sea, embodying the Renaissance revival of classical beauty.

title: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
description: Sailing for Spain, he makes landfall on an island he names San Salvador.

title: Fall of Granada ends the Reconquista
description: The surrender of the last Moorish emir completes the Christian reconquest of Spain after nearly eight centuries.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches India
description: Rounding Africa, the Portuguese captain anchors at Calicut, opening the all-sea spice route that will reshape global trade.

title: Montezuma II crowned Aztec emperor
description: The warrior-priest Montezuma II ascends the throne of an Aztec Empire at the zenith of its power and tribute.

title: Leonardo begins the Mona Lisa
description: Leonardo da Vinci starts the enigmatic portrait that becomes the most famous painting of the Italian Renaissance.

title: Luther nails the 95 Theses
description: In Wittenberg. The Protestant Reformation splits Western Christianity.

title: Cortes enters Tenochtitlan
description: Hernan Cortes and his conquistadors march into the Aztec capital as guests of Montezuma, beginning the empire's destruction.

title: Suleiman the Magnificent takes the throne
description: Suleiman begins a reign that will carry Ottoman arms to the gates of Vienna and bring the empire to its golden age.

title: Magellan killed in the Philippines
description: Ferdinand Magellan dies in battle on Mactan, but his expedition sails on to complete the first circumnavigation of the globe.

title: Babur wins the Battle of Panipat
description: With artillery and cavalry Babur routs the Delhi Sultanate and founds the Mughal Empire in India.

title: Ottoman siege of Vienna
description: Suleiman's army reaches the walls of Vienna, marking the high tide of Ottoman expansion into central Europe.

title: Pizarro captures the Inca Atahualpa
description: At Cajamarca a small Spanish force ambushes and seizes the Inca emperor, beginning the conquest of the Andean empire.

title: Henry VIII breaks with Rome
description: The Act of Supremacy makes the king head of the Church of England, severing the realm from papal authority.

title: Copernicus publishes the heliocentric model
description: On his deathbed Nicolaus Copernicus publishes his treatise placing the Sun, not the Earth, at the center of the heavens.

title: Potosi silver mines opened
description: Spanish miners begin working the mountain of Potosi, whose silver will flood world markets and fund the Habsburg empire.

title: Akbar becomes Mughal emperor
description: The thirteen-year-old Akbar inherits the Mughal throne and will expand it into a vast empire famed for religious tolerance.

title: Battle of Talikota shatters Vijayanagara
description: A coalition of Deccan sultanates crushes the Vijayanagara army and sacks its capital, ending South India's great Hindu empire.

title: Battle of Lepanto
description: A Holy League fleet destroys the Ottoman navy in one of history's last great galley battles, checking Ottoman sea power.

title: Gregorian calendar introduced
description: Pope Gregory XIII reforms the calendar to correct the drift of the seasons, dropping ten days from October.

title: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
description: English fireships and Atlantic storms scatter Philip II's great fleet, marking the rise of English sea power.

title: English East India Company chartered
description: Elizabeth I grants a company of London merchants a monopoly on eastern trade, seeding an empire built on commerce.

title: Battle of Sekigahara
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu crushed his rivals in a single decisive day, opening the path to a shogunate that would rule Japan for 250 years.

title: Kepler Becomes Imperial Mathematician
description: Johannes Kepler inherited Tycho Brahe's precise observations in Prague, data that would let him unravel the elliptical orbits of the planets.

title: Tokugawa Shogunate Established
description: Ieyasu took the title of shogun and founded Edo as his capital, inaugurating an era of isolation and internal peace.

title: Don Quixote Published
description: Miguel de Cervantes released the first part of his tale of a deluded knight, often called the first modern novel.

title: Jamestown Founded
description: English settlers established the first permanent English colony in North America on a malarial Virginia riverbank.

title: Galileo's Telescopic Observations
description: Galileo turned an improved telescope to the night sky from Padua, soon discovering Jupiter's moons and lunar mountains.

title: Assassination of Henry IV
description: A Catholic fanatic stabbed the tolerant French king in his carriage on a Paris street, ending the reign that had healed the wars of religion.

title: Romanov Dynasty Begins
description: Sixteen-year-old Michael Romanov was elected tsar, ending the chaotic Time of Troubles and founding a dynasty that lasted three centuries.

title: Thirty Years' War Erupts
description: Protestant nobles threw imperial envoys from a Prague castle window, igniting a continental war that devastated central Europe.

title: Mayflower Lands at Plymouth
description: English Puritan separatists signed a civil compact aboard ship before founding their colony on the Massachusetts coast.

title: Reign of Shah Jahan Begins
description: Shah Jahan ascended the Mughal throne, ushering in the empire's golden age of architecture and the eventual Taj Mahal.

title: Taj Mahal Construction Begins
description: Shah Jahan ordered a white marble mausoleum for his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal on the banks of the Yamuna at Agra.

title: Galileo Condemned by the Inquisition
description: The Roman Inquisition forced Galileo to recant his defense of a sun-centered cosmos and sentenced him to house arrest.

title: Qing Dynasty Proclaimed
description: Hong Taiji renamed his Manchu state the Qing at Mukden, laying claim to the Mandate of Heaven over China.

title: Descartes Publishes the Discourse on Method
description: Rene Descartes argued for systematic doubt and declared 'I think, therefore I am,' founding modern rationalist philosophy.

title: Fall of the Ming Dynasty
description: Rebel forces seized Beijing and the last Ming emperor hanged himself, after which the Manchus marched in to establish Qing rule.

title: Peace of Westphalia
description: Treaties signed at Munster and Osnabruck ended the Thirty Years' War and enshrined the principle of sovereign states.

title: Execution of Charles I
description: The English Parliament beheaded its king outside the Banqueting House, a revolutionary act that briefly abolished the monarchy.

title: Dutch Settle the Cape of Good Hope
description: Jan van Riebeeck established a supply station for the Dutch East India Company, seeding European settlement in South Africa.

title: Aurangzeb Seizes the Mughal Throne
description: After imprisoning his father and killing his brothers, the austere Aurangzeb began a reign that expanded and then overstretched the empire.

title: Great Plague of London
description: Bubonic plague swept through London's crowded streets, killing roughly a quarter of the city's population in a single year.

title: Ashanti Empire Founded
description: Osei Tutu united the Akan clans around the Golden Stool at Kumasi, forging a powerful empire in the forests of present-day Ghana.

title: Siege of Vienna Lifted
description: A Polish-led Christian army routed the Ottoman host at the gates of Vienna, marking the high tide of Turkish expansion in Europe.

title: Newton's Principia Published
description: Isaac Newton set out his laws of motion and universal gravitation, unifying the heavens and earth under a single mathematics.

title: Glorious Revolution
description: Parliament deposed James II and invited William and Mary to rule, establishing constitutional limits on the English crown.

title: Treaty of Karlowitz
description: The Ottomans ceded Hungary and other lands to the Habsburgs, the empire's first great territorial retreat in Europe.

title: Act of Union Creates Great Britain
description: The parliaments of England and Scotland merged into a single Kingdom of Great Britain under one crown and legislature.

title: Hotak Revolt Topples Safavid Rule in the East
description: Mirwais Hotak led an Afghan uprising at Kandahar against Safavid overlords, beginning the unraveling of Persia's Safavid dynasty.

title: Fall of Isfahan
description: Afghan besiegers starved out the Safavid capital, effectively ending a dynasty that had ruled Persia for over two centuries.

title: Death of Peter the Great
description: The reforming tsar who built St. Petersburg and westernized Russia died, leaving an empire transformed into a European power.

title: Linnaeus Publishes Systema Naturae
description: Carl Linnaeus introduced his hierarchical system for classifying all living things, the foundation of modern biological taxonomy.

title: Nader Shah Sacks Delhi
description: The Persian conqueror plundered the Mughal capital and carried off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

title: Montesquieu's Spirit of the Laws
description: Montesquieu argued for the separation of governmental powers, a cornerstone idea for later constitutional democracies.

title: Lisbon Earthquake
description: A massive quake, fire, and tsunami destroyed Lisbon on All Saints' Day, shaking Enlightenment faith in a benevolent order.

title: Battle of Plassey
description: Robert Clive's East India Company forces defeated the Nawab of Bengal through bribery and battle, beginning British dominion in India.

title: Rousseau's The Social Contract
description: Jean-Jacques Rousseau opened with 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains,' shaping revolutionary ideas of popular sovereignty.

title: Watt Patents the Improved Steam Engine
description: James Watt patented a separate condenser that made steam power efficient, a key spark of the Industrial Revolution.

title: US Declaration of Independence
description: Philadelphia. Thirteen colonies declare separation from Britain.

title: Adam Smith's Wealth of Nations
description: Adam Smith described how self-interest and free markets guide prosperity, founding the discipline of modern economics.

title: Siege of Yorktown
description: Washington's army and a French fleet trapped Cornwallis in Virginia, forcing the surrender that effectively won American independence.

title: Storming of the Bastille
description: The French Revolution begins; the old regime will not survive the decade.

title: Haitian Revolution Begins
description: Enslaved Africans rose up across the plantations of Saint-Domingue, launching the only successful large-scale slave revolt in history.

title: Execution of Louis XVI
description: The French Revolution sent its king to the guillotine before a Paris crowd, shocking the monarchies of Europe.

title: Jenner Publishes Smallpox Vaccination
description: Edward Jenner demonstrated that cowpox inoculation protected against deadly smallpox, inaugurating the science of vaccination.

title: Haitian Independence Proclaimed
description: Jean-Jacques Dessalines declared Haiti a free nation, the first independent Black republic born of a slave revolution.

title: Napoleon Crowned Emperor
description: Napoleon Bonaparte placed the crown on his own head at Notre-Dame, transforming the revolutionary republic into an empire.

title: Sokoto Caliphate Jihad Begins
description: The scholar Usman dan Fodio launched a religious revolution across the Hausa lands, founding a vast Islamic caliphate.

title: Britain Abolishes the Slave Trade
description: Parliament outlawed the transatlantic slave trade in British ships, a major blow to the Atlantic commerce in human beings.

title: Mexican War of Independence Begins
description: The priest Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell at Dolores and called the people to rise against Spanish rule.

title: Bolivar's Victory at Boyaca
description: Simon Bolivar routed the Spanish army near a bridge in the Andes, securing the liberation of New Granada.

title: Battle of Ayacucho
description: Patriot forces under Sucre shattered the last royalist army in South America, sealing independence across the continent.

title: Auspicious Incident Destroys the Janissaries
description: Sultan Mahmud II violently abolished the rebellious Janissary corps, clearing the way for Ottoman military modernization.

title: Great Trek of the Boers
description: Dutch-descended farmers migrated inland from the British Cape in ox wagons, founding new republics in the African interior.

title: First Opium War Begins
description: China's seizure of British opium at Canton triggered a war that would force open its ports and cede Hong Kong.

title: Revolutions Sweep Europe
description: A wave of liberal and nationalist uprisings erupted across the continent, shaking monarchies from Paris to Vienna to Berlin.

title: Great Exhibition opens in the Crystal Palace
description: London's glass-and-iron Crystal Palace drew millions to a global showcase of industrial machinery and manufactured wonders.

title: Perry's black ships reach Edo Bay
description: Commodore Perry's steam-powered squadron anchored off Uraga and forced Japan to end two centuries of isolation.

title: Indian Rebellion against the East India Company
description: A mutiny of sepoys at Meerut spread into a vast uprising that would end Company rule and bring India under the Crown.

title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
description: From Down House, Darwin laid out natural selection and reshaped humanity's understanding of life itself.

title: Emancipation of the serfs in Russia
description: Tsar Alexander II signed the edict freeing over twenty million serfs from bondage to the land.

title: Emancipation Proclamation and the American Civil War
description: Lincoln declared enslaved people in rebel states to be free, recasting the war as a struggle for abolition.

title: Marx publishes Das Kapital
description: Karl Marx's sweeping critique of capitalist production gave the industrial working class a new political language.

title: Suez Canal opens between seas
description: The canal joining the Mediterranean and Red Sea cut thousands of miles from the route between Europe and Asia.

title: Transcontinental Railroad completed at Promontory
description: A golden spike driven in Utah linked America's coasts by rail and opened the continental interior.

title: German unification proclaimed at Versailles
description: Bismarck's princes crowned Wilhelm I emperor in the Hall of Mirrors, forging a unified German Reich.

title: Italian unification completed with Rome as capital
description: With the capital moved to a newly seized Rome, the long Risorgimento finally bound the peninsula into one kingdom.

title: Bell patents the telephone
description: Alexander Graham Bell transmitted speech over a wire in Boston, inaugurating instant voice communication.

title: Berlin Conference carves up Africa
description: European powers met in Berlin to partition the African continent among themselves without a single African present.

title: Eiffel Tower crowns the Paris Exposition
description: Gustave Eiffel's wrought-iron tower rose over the World's Fair as the tallest structure on Earth.

title: Ethiopia routs Italy at Adwa
description: Emperor Menelik II's army shattered an invading Italian force, securing Ethiopia's independence against colonization.

title: Curies isolate radium and polonium
description: Marie and Pierre Curie extracted new radioactive elements from pitchblende in a cramped Paris shed.

title: Marconi sends signal across the Atlantic
description: Guglielmo Marconi received a faint wireless signal in Newfoundland, proving radio could span oceans.

title: Wright brothers achieve powered flight
description: At Kitty Hawk the Wright Flyer lifted off the dunes, making humanity's first sustained powered flight.

title: Einstein's miracle year of physics
description: A Bern patent clerk published relativity and the quantum of light, overturning the foundations of physics.

title: Mexican Revolution erupts against Diaz
description: Madero's call to arms ignited a decade of revolution that toppled a long dictatorship and remade Mexico.

title: Amundsen reaches the South Pole
description: Roald Amundsen's Norwegian party planted a flag at the geographic South Pole, winning the polar race.

title: Xinhai Revolution ends China's empire
description: An uprising at Wuchang swept away the Qing dynasty and founded the Republic of China.

title: Titanic sinks on her maiden voyage
description: The great liner struck an iceberg and foundered, carrying more than fifteen hundred souls into the cold Atlantic.

title: Assassination at Sarajevo sparks the Great War
description: The killing of Archduke Franz Ferdinand set the alliances of Europe tumbling into the First World War.

title: Bolshevik Revolution seizes Petrograd
description: Lenin's Bolsheviks stormed the Winter Palace and launched the world's first communist state.

title: Spanish flu pandemic sweeps the globe
description: An influenza strain tore across the war-weary world, killing tens of millions on every continent.

title: Treaty of Versailles redraws the world
description: The victors imposed terms on Germany and reshaped empires, sowing grievances that would ripen into another war.

title: Mussolini's March on Rome
description: Fascist blackshirts marched on the capital and brought Mussolini to power, the first fascist regime in Europe.

title: Wall Street Crash begins the Great Depression
description: The stock market collapse in New York plunged the industrial world into a decade of mass unemployment.

title: Gandhi's Salt March defies British rule
description: Gandhi walked to the sea at Dandi to make salt in defiance of colonial law, galvanizing mass nonviolent resistance.

title: Hitler seizes power in Germany
description: Appointed chancellor, Adolf Hitler swiftly dismantled the Weimar Republic and built the Nazi dictatorship.

title: Germany invades Poland, igniting World War II
description: The Wehrmacht's blitzkrieg across Poland drew Britain and France into a second global war.

title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
description: First and only wartime uses of nuclear weapons. Japan surrenders days later.

title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
description: A single uranium bomb destroyed Hiroshima, ushering in the nuclear age and hastening Japan's surrender.

title: Partition of India and Pakistan
description: British India split into two nations amid independence, triggering mass migration and communal bloodshed.

title: Apartheid becomes law in South Africa
description: The National Party institutionalized racial segregation, binding South Africa in decades of apartheid rule.

title: Mao proclaims the People's Republic of China
description: From Tiananmen, Mao Zedong declared the communist victory and the founding of the People's Republic.

title: Watson and Crick reveal the DNA double helix
description: At Cambridge the structure of DNA was unveiled, exposing the molecular code of heredity.

title: Ghana wins independence from Britain
description: Kwame Nkrumah led Ghana to become the first sub-Saharan colony to break free, lighting Africa's decolonization.

title: Sputnik opens the Space Age
description: The Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite from Baikonur, startling the world and starting the space race.

title: Gagarin becomes the first human in space
description: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1, the first person to leave the planet and return.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis brings the world to the brink
description: The discovery of Soviet missiles in Cuba pushed the superpowers to the edge of nuclear war before a tense standoff.

title: Apollo 11 lunar landing
description: Launched from Kennedy Space Center. Armstrong and Aldrin walk the Moon.

title: Apollo 11 lands humans on the Moon
description: Armstrong and Aldrin stepped onto the Sea of Tranquility, the first humans to walk on another world.

title: OPEC oil embargo shocks the global economy
description: Arab oil producers cut exports to the West, quadrupling prices and exposing the world's dependence on petroleum.

title: Iranian Revolution establishes an Islamic Republic
description: Ayatollah Khomeini's return toppled the Shah and founded a theocratic state in Tehran.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: Crowds breached the Berlin Wall, collapsing the Iron Curtain and ending the division of Europe.

title: Soviet Union dissolves
description: The hammer-and-sickle came down over the Kremlin as fifteen republics emerged from the fallen USSR.

title: World Wide Web opened to the public
description: At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee released the Web to the world, launching the age of the internet.

title: Mandela elected in South Africa's first free vote
description: Nelson Mandela won the presidency in all-race elections, ending apartheid and inaugurating a democratic South Africa.

title: Indian Ocean tsunami devastates coastlines
description: A massive undersea quake off Sumatra unleashed waves that killed over two hundred thousand across a dozen nations.

title: COVID-19 declared a global pandemic
description: A novel coronavirus first identified in Wuhan swept the planet, shutting down economies and societies worldwide.

title: Generative AI reaches the mainstream
description: Large language models like ChatGPT crossed into everyday use, marking a new era of artificial intelligence.
